title: Bug: Tidy up (Alt+T) in eagle view leaves a half-height column when a terminal is not launched yet
seam: src/lib/eagleLayout.ts and the eagle view Tidy up in src/components/shared/MultiProjectView.tsx
story: In eagle view, Tidy up used to arrange only the launched terminals as columns. A card waiting to be launched had nowhere to go, so it was squeezed under one terminal and cut that column in half. Now the card counts as a tile and gets its own full-height column, and it keeps that column once you launch it. With terminals only, Tidy up behaves exactly as before.

checks.criterion: Tidy up puts every tile, cards included, in one row of full-height columns of equal width, in reading order, and no terminal is cut.
checks.steps: Open a made-up project 'demo-proj' and switch to eagle view. Launch two terminals. Click Add terminal once and leave the new card unlaunched. Press Alt+T. Repeat with the top-bar Tidy up button.
checks.expected: Three full-height columns of equal width, the two terminals then the card, left to right. Nothing is stacked or cut in half.

checks.criterion: A card launched after Tidy up keeps its full-height column.
checks.steps: Do the setup of eagle-view/tidy-with-card and press Alt+T. Click Launch Session on the card.
checks.expected: The new terminal fills the card's right-hand column at full height, and the other two columns do not change.

checks.criterion: With too many tiles, cards counted, Tidy up falls back to the automatic grid.
checks.steps: In eagle view, launch nine terminals. Add two cards and leave them unlaunched. Press Alt+T.
checks.expected: The usual square-ish automatic grid, not a row of columns.
